channel.description: math.NT updates on the arXiv.org e-print archive.

item.title: A law of the iterated logarithm for random multiplicative functions on integers with a large prime factor
item.description: arXiv:2610.40707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers. We investigate the almost sure fluctuations of the restricted sum $M^{>}(x)=\sum_{n\le x;~ P(n)>x^{1/2}}f(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime factor of $n$. With $Q(x)$ being the conditional variance of $M^{>}(x)$ given the values of $f$ at primes not exceeding $x^{1/2}$, we prove that, almost surely, the upper and lower limits of $M^{>}(x)(2Q(x)\log\log Q(x))^{-1/2}$ as $x\to\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, respectively. Furthermore, it is shown that the almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$.
item.dc:creator: Dariusz Buraczewski, Alexander Iksanov

item.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
item.description: arXiv:2610.40815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Alessandr\`i, Jiazhi He

item.title: A Local Fourier-Transform Proof of Offen's Spherical Transfer Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.40819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E/F$ be an unramified quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic zero and odd residual characteristic. Offen proved that, on the full spherical space of nondegenerate Hermitian matrices, equality of the Hironaka and Satake transforms implies Jacquet--Ye matching. We give a purely local proof of this theorem. The argument combines Jacquet's compatibility of matching with Fourier transform, the Godement--Jacquet functional equation, and Hironaka's scalar functional equation for Hermitian zeta integrals. The local proof recovers Jacquet's spherical-Hecke fundamental lemma from the unit case.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Mao, Chen Wan

item.title: Erd\H{o}s--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erd\H{o}s--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff.
item.dc:creator: Andres Ventas

item.title: Clusters of primes revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.41113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the generalized Rayleigh quotient optimization problem related to the Maynard-Tao sieve with the goal of finding a more efficient function basis. We demonstrate that a family based on products of reciprocals, previously used in asymptotic estimates for $H_m = \liminf_{n \to \infty}(p_{n+m}-p_n)$, provides results that are close to the theoretical limits of the sieve across many regimes. In particular, we establish $H_2 \leq 31 \, 140$, $H_3 \leq 2 \, 560 \, 022$, $H_4 \leq 193 \, 672 \, 056$, and $H_5 \leq 13 \, 659 \, 045 \, 840$. We also show that, as $k \to \infty$, the related variational quantity $M_k$, introduced by Maynard, satisfies the lower bound $M_k \geq \log k - 0.273572 + o(1)$.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Lewulis

item.title: A spectral theory of zeta functions of function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.41115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Hilbert spaces constructed from the Weil quadratic form associated with the zeta function of a curve over a finite field, together with self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator on these spaces. For a distinguished family of these extensions, we prove that the eigenvalues converge to the ordinates of the zeros of the zeta function and that the corresponding entire spectral functions, after normalization, converge locally uniformly to an infinite product determined by these zeros. These limits occur as the interval parameter approaches a finite endpoint, rather than infinity as in the setting of the Riemann zeta function. We also realize the global Hilbert space through the Rosati trace pairing and show that translation by $\log q$ is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by normalized Frobenius. This provides a geometric model for the analogous analytic constructions associated with the Riemann zeta function.
item.dc:creator: Masatoshi Suzuki

item.title: Weil Operators and Remainders of Anderson Generating Functions over a Punctured Projective Line
item.description: arXiv:2610.41131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A_\rho$ be the coordinate ring of the projective line over $\Fq$ with a closed point of degree $N$ removed. We give finite formulas for higher Weil operators in a basis of Riemann--Roch spaces, which recover the formulas of Hu--Ou--Yang when $N=1$. We identifythese operators with representatives of the residue Casimir tensors and obtain a determinant formula for the Weil pairing, relative to a chosen determinant realization. For a normalized rank-one Drinfeld module, we compute the remainder of its Anderson generating function modulo any nonconstant $p\in A_\rho$. The formula includes multiple zeros and a zero at the ordinary point at infinity. Its last coefficient is a nonzero scalar multiple of an exponential division value. When $(p)$ is a finite principal prime, a value of the associated special function at one zero of $p$ generates the torsion field after adjoining that zero. We give an explicit $q$-linear formula recovering a torsion generator from this value. We also specialize the evaluation theorem of Gazda--Maurischat and compute the different as the principal ideal $(\partial_xp)$.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Xiao-Min Huang, Guorui Ma

item.title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant \Gamma_{1,4} = 8
item.description: arXiv:2610.41223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants \Gamma_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Vineet Kahlon

item.title: Vector Valued Katok-Sarnak Formulas
item.description: arXiv:2610.41298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a version of the Katok-Sarnak formula linking twisted traces of scalar valued Maass cusp forms for $\Gamma_0(N)$ with $N$ square-free to Fourier coefficients of vector valued Maass cusp forms for the metaplectic group $\operatorname{Mp}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and the Weil representation associated to a lattice of signature $(2,1)$. We prove this by computing the Fourier coefficients of the vector valued Siegel and Millson theta lift of a scalar valued newform by two different methods and comparing the results.
item.dc:creator: Rebekka Strathausen

item.title: Kloosterman Sums and Pl\"ucker Height Zeta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish nontrivial bounds for Kloosterman sums over $p$-adic fields associated with the longest Weyl element on arbitrary split reductive groups, at arbitrary level. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions (of Whittaker models) for all such groups.
item.dc:creator: Li Cai, Jingsong Chai, Yadi Liu, Mingyu Yang

item.title: Primes and the M\"obius function over quadratic polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.41356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for the number of primes $p\leq X$ of the form $n^2+h$ for almost all $h \leq X^{1/2-o(1)}$. We prove that, for almost all $h \leq X^{2/5}$, the number of primes satisfies a correct-order lower bound. We also show cancellation of the M\"obius function over $n^2+h$ for almost all $h < X^{1/2-o(1)}$.
item.dc:creator: Lasse Grimmelt, Jori Merikoski, Mayank Pandey, Alexandru Pascadi

item.title: Twisted second moments of Dirichlet $L$-functions with applications to weighted one-level density
item.description: arXiv:2610.41394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function in the $t$-aspect. This is a generalization of Selberg's asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta function. As an application, we observe the change and the stability of the weighted one-level density of zeros of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function.
item.dc:creator: Naoto Inumaru, Shingo Sugiyama

item.title: Irrationality of values of $L$-functions for real Dirichlet characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.41458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\chi$ be a non-trivial real Dirichlet character and $s$ be a sufficiently large integer. In this paper, we prove that among the first $s$ non-critical special values of the Dirichlet $L$-function associated with $\chi$ at least $c\sqrt{\frac{s}{\log s}}$ are irrational, where $c$ is a constant independent of $s$. This is a substantial improvement on work of Fischler when $4$ divides the conductor of $\chi$. Otherwise, our constant improves on work of Mistiaen. The proof adapts some techniques of Lai and Yu for odd zeta values to the case of $L$-functions. The lack of positivity arguments is overcome by applying an irrationality criterion by Lai and Sprang originating from the $p$-adic setting.
item.dc:creator: Veekesh Kumar, Riccardo Tosi

item.title: On sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of theta quotients
item.description: arXiv:2610.41569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou on sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of infinite products, we study two families of theta quotients and their positive integral powers. We determine asymptotic formulas for their Fourier coefficients and use them to obtain explicit eventual periodic sign patterns. Our results provide new instances of the sign phenomena observed by Schlosser and Zhou and illustrate how dominant cusps determine the resulting sign patterns. These results were formalized and verified in Lean by AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Koustav Banerjee, Kathrin Bringmann, Bernhard Heim, Ben Kane

item.title: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.41573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Th\'el\`ene, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Gambardella, Nguyen Manh Linh

item.title: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.41600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the shifts $\zeta(s+id_j\tau)$, $1\le j\le n$, are jointly universal for any nonzero real parameters $d_j$ with pairwise distinct absolute values. These restrictions are best possible. As an immediate consequence, we obtain generalized strong recurrence for arbitrary finite families of nonzero real parameters. Our proof uses Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem and a new variant of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem.
item.dc:creator: {\L}ukasz Pa\'nkowski

item.title: Estimates of Lucas series and expansions in non-integer bases
item.description: arXiv:2610.41658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Special Fibonacci and Lucas type expansions proved useful to ``correct'' some theorems on the number of expansions in non-integer bases \cite{BaiKomLor2021, KomLorPed2024, KomLorPed2025}. The proof of a key lemma was non-constructive. It was made constructive in the Fibonacci case by giving a precise estimate of the growth of the partial sums of the series of the inverses of the Fibonacci numbers \cite{KomPed2025}. In this paper we extend this result to the general case.
item.dc:creator: Vilmos Komornik, Marco Pedicini

item.title: On the modularity of residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2
item.description: arXiv:2610.41764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use a new version of the Taylor--Wiles method, based on a tame analogue of the techniques introduced by Skinner--Wiles, to prove new modularity theorems for residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2 over totally real fields.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Dotto, Jack A. Thorne

item.title: A conjecture on Galois groups and large fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.41843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a field such that $p$ is prime to the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$, in the sense that $p$ does not divide the degree of any finite Galois extension of $K$. We conjecture that $K$ is large in the sense of Pop: any smooth algebraic curve $C$ over $K$ with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points. This conjecture would have some consequences in mathematical logic. For instance, it would imply the expected classification of stable fields of positive characteristic. We give some weak evidence for this conjecture. Specifically, suppose that $K$ is a perfect field and $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$ is prime to $p$. Then every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ has Zariski dense $K$-rational points, and if $C$ is a smooth curve of genus less than $7-p$ with at least one $K$-rational point, then $C$ has infinitely many $K$-rational points.
item.dc:creator: Will Johnson

item.title: Central values of additive twists of automorphic $L$-series
item.description: arXiv:2610.42008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n \rho(n)e^{2\pi i n x}/n^s$, where $\rho(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $\phi$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $\Gamma\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathfrak{b}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ represent a cusp of $\Gamma$. Ordering the orbit $\Gamma\mathfrak{b}$ by increasing denominators, we prove that the values $L(x,1/2)$ for $x\in\Gamma\mathfrak{b}$, suitably normalized, become equidistributed according to a standard complex Gaussian law, under natural assumptions on the Laplace eigenvalue of $\phi$. Previously this was known either when $\Gamma=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ or when $\phi$ is associated to a holomorphic cusp form. This applies in particular to central values at $s=1/2$ of additive twists of Maass form $L$-functions $\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda(n)e^{2\pi i n x}/n^s$, or to the Dirichlet-theta series $\sum_{n\geq1}\chi(n)e^{2\pi i n^2 x}/n^s$.
item.dc:creator: Sandro Bettin, Sandro Bettin, Jungwon Lee

item.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.42022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.
item.dc:creator: Yassine El Kaouni

item.title: On the Iwasawa invariants of admissible quadratic twists of elliptic curves at ordinary Eisenstein primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.42137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Iwasawa $\mu$- and $\lambda$-invariants of quadratic twists of rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes $p\geq 3$. We verify Greenberg's $\mu=0$ conjecture for all such twists, which gives an Euler system free proof of Mazur's cotorsion conjecture, and study the $\lambda$-invariants when the twist is admissible in the sense of [GV00]. As a consequence, we prove the cyclotomic Iwasawa Main Conjecture and obtain the $p$-part BSD formulae in rank $0$ for admissible twists under mild conditions, covering many elliptic curves of potentially ordinary reduction.
item.dc:creator: Mulun Yin

item.title: Descent and Decomposability of Algebras of Exponent 2 in characteristic 2
item.description: arXiv:2610.40673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define an invariant of central simple algebras of degree 8 and exponent 2 over fields of characteristic 2. It is built from the discriminant Pfister forms of symplectic involutions, takes values in a quotient of the third part of the graded group associated to the fundamental filtration of the Witt group of quadratic forms, and vanishes on tensor products of three quaternion algebras, thus giving a necessary condition for decomposability. Variants of the consctuction yield necessary and sufficient conditions for a biquaternion algebra to descend from a quadratic extension of the base field, and for a quaternion algebra to descent from a biquadratic extension that is not purely inseparable. Our results extend known results both in characteristic 2 and in characteristic different from 2, see the introduction. Using residue maps for quadratic forms, we show that these invariants do not vanish in general, and we give an explicit central simple algebra of degree 8 and exponent 2 with nonzero invariant, which is therefore indecomposable. As explained in the appendix, the purely inseparable case is quite different; in particular, a quaternion algebra descents if and only if its Brauer class also does.
item.dc:creator: Anne Qu\'eguiner-Mathieu, Jean-Pierre Tignol

item.title: Four runners that are barely lonely
item.description: arXiv:2610.40694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For positive integers $v_1,\dots,v_n$ let $\mathrm{ML}(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\max_t\min_i\|v_it\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance to the nearest integer. Kravitz asked which values below $1/n$ occur. For $n=4$, Jain and Kravitz showed that the values below $1/4$ are $m/(4m+2)$, $m\ge2$, up to finitely many undetermined exceptions. We settle the four-runner case completely. A primitive quadruple has $\mathrm{ML}<1/4$ if and only if it is, up to order, $\{1,2,3,4k\}$, or $\{x,y,x+y,x+2y\}$ with $\gcd(x,y)=1$ and $y\not\equiv x,2x\pmod 4$, or $\{1,3,4,14\}$. The values below $1/4$ are exactly $m/(4m+2)$ with $m\ge2$, $m\ne3$, so $3/14$ is the only exception, and Conjecture 4.1 of Fan and Sun holds. A density lemma bounds the length of a quadruple on neither critical subtorus by $512$, and an exact search over 800,816,099 quadruples completes the proof. The same method shows that the two-dimensional subtori of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^4$ with loneliness below $2/5$ take exactly the three-runner values in that range, which between $1/3$ and $2/5$ are the fractions $p/q$ with $1\le 2q-5p\le 4$. Hence the accumulation points of the four-runner spectrum in $(0,2/5]$ are the three-runner values there, as Giri and Kravitz conjectured, and $9/25$ is not the loneliness of a two-dimensional subtorus. For every $n$, assuming the conjecture for $n-1$ and $n-2$ speeds, we prove $\mathrm{ML}(v)>1/n-(n(n-1))^{n-2}/(2|v|)$, which is sharp in $|v|$, and that every $n$-tuple with $\mathrm{ML}<1/n$ and $|v|\ge n(n(n-1))^{2n-4}$ lies on a two-dimensional subtorus of loneliness $1/n$. This answers a question of Cordella. For five speeds, a two-dimensional subtorus of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^5$ with loneliness below $2/9$ is the product of a coordinate circle with the circle of $\{1,2,3,4\}$ or $\{1,3,4,7\}$. We also give infinitely many subtori whose maximizers lie off every circle with a repeated speed.
item.dc:creator: Hyunjun Yi, Karam Gill, Bryan Bu

item.title: A Diophantine generalization of Fourier's irrationality trick
item.description: arXiv:2610.40698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit Fourier's method for proving the irrationality of $e$ and generalize it into a unified Diophantine framework, which applies to a broad class of series with bounded or mildly growing integer numerators, and suitably growing, divisible denominators. Using integer linear forms, we establish a general criterion that recovers classical irrationality results while also generating new ones within a single structural approach.
item.dc:creator: Archan Chattopadhyay, Chandan Chattopadhyay

item.title: The complexity of tilting
item.description: arXiv:2610.41064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $\phi$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $\phi^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $\phi^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $\phi$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the L\'evy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.
item.dc:creator: Leo Gitin

item.title: Limit theorems for cuspidal orbits on Fuchsian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.41973v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma\subset \operatorname{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ be discrete, co-finite with cusps, and let ${\frak b}\in \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a cusp of $\Gamma$. Let $f: \Gamma{\frak b} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a quantum modular form in the sense that the maps $$ \phi_\gamma(x) = f(x) - f(\gamma x) \qquad (x\in \Gamma{\frak b}, \gamma \in \Gamma) $$ extend to H\"older-regular functions. Under bounded moments assumptions of the shape $\sum_n n^{-2} \int |\phi_{\gamma^n}(x)|^\alpha d x < \infty$ for some $\alpha>0$ and every fixed parabolic element $\gamma\in \Gamma$, we prove asymptotic formulas for the characteristic functions of the values $f(x)$ for $x\in \Gamma{\frak b}$, ordered by growing denominators. These yield Gaussian limits when $\alpha>2$ and other stable limit laws under suitable further assumptions. This generalizes to Fuchsian groups the work of Baladi-Vall\'ee on rational orbits of the Gauss map. In companion papers, we use this result, and in particular its flexible assumptions on $\phi_\gamma$, to deduce limit theorems for automorphic $L$-series at the central point. One ingredient in our proof is a particular cuspidal acceleration of the Bowen-Series map, whose inverse branches admit a convenient parametrization, and for which we describe explicitly a natural extension.
item.dc:creator: Sandro Bettin, Sary Drappeau, Jungwon Lee

item.title: On the surjectivity of Galois representations attached to Drinfeld $A$-modules of rank $2$
item.description: arXiv:2502.19084v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, where $q$ is a prime power and let $A:= \mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$ and $F:= \mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. By~\cite{PR09}, the adelic image of the Galois representation attached to a generic Drinfeld $A$-module $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$ satisfying $\mathrm{End}_{\bar{F }}(\varphi)=\varphi(A)$ is open, and determining when it is surjective remains a subtle problem. To resolve this question, in this article, we study the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic surjectivity of the Galois representations attached to $\varphi$, where $\mathfrak{p} \in \Omega_A:= \mathrm{Spec}(A) \setminus \{ (0) \}$. There are two directions to investigate this problem: one by fixing the prime $\mathfrak{p}$, and the other by fixing $\varphi$. In the horizontal direction, for a fixed $\mathfrak{p} \in \Omega_A$, we give explicit and easily verifiable conditions on Drinfeld $A$-modules $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$ which ensure the surjectivity of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic Galois representation $\rho_{\varphi,\mathfrak{p}}$. This work extends~\cite{Ray24} to arbitrary $\mathfrak{p}$, and, for $\mathfrak{p}=(T)$, recovers the results of~\textit{loc. cit.} under weaker hypotheses. In the vertical direction, we show that for a fixed Drinfeld $A$-module $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$, whose coefficients satisfy certain congruence and valuation conditions, the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic Galois representation $\rho_{\varphi,\mathfrak{p}}$ is surjective for all $\mathfrak{p} \in \Omega_A$. This recovers the example of \cite{Zyw11} and yields new examples beyond those considered in \cite{Zyw25}. As a consequence, we obtain the surjectivity of the associated adelic Galois representation.
item.dc:creator: Narasimha Kumar, Dwipanjana Shit

item.title: Period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$
item.description: arXiv:2506.20942v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the modular symbol approach, we prove the rationality and period relations for certain critical values of Rankin-Selberg L-functions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$ over any number field that contains a CM field.
item.dc:creator: Yubo Jin, Jian-Shu Li, Dongwen Liu, Binyong Sun

item.title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers I. Analytic Rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2609.14202v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathscr L$ denote the set of Liouville numbers. We prove a local arithmetic rigidity theorem for real-analytic functions. If $U\subset\mathbb R$ is an open interval and $f:U\to\mathbb R$ is real-analytic with $f(\mathscr L\cap U)\subseteq\mathscr L$, then $f$ is the restriction to $U$ of a rational function in $\mathbb R(x)$. Quantitatively, there exists an absolute constant $\tau>2$ such that, for every nonrational real-analytic function $f$ and every nonempty open subinterval $V\subset U$, the set of $\xi\in V\cap\mathscr L$ satisfying $\mu(f(\xi))\leq\tau$ contains a Cantor set. As a consequence, every entire function $F:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ satisfying $F(\mathscr L)\subseteq \mathscr L$ is a polynomial with real coefficients. This gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Mahler in 1984. The proof develops a two-height counting estimate for rational approximation to analytic graphs, treating source and target denominators separately, and combines it with a nested construction producing Liouville inputs whose images have uniformly bounded irrationality exponent.
item.dc:creator: Diego Marques

item.title: Ray class groups in the cyclotomic tower
item.description: arXiv:2610.17649v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty finite set of rational primes different from $p$. In the cyclotomic tower $\mathbb{Q}(\mu_{p^{n+1}})$, we determine the kernels of the natural maps from the minus $p$-primary ray class groups, with modulus the product of the primes above $\Sigma$, to the corresponding ordinary minus $p$-primary class groups. We give their character components and elementary divisors at every finite layer, including the layers before splitting stabilizes. In the norm inverse limit, we obtain an explicit integral cyclic decomposition of the local module modulo the single diagonal global Tate module. Its coinvariants recover the finite local kernels. Together with ordinary class-group control, this gives exact control for the minus ray class groups. We identify the local Frobenius factors with Bernoulli regularization factors. For nonexceptional characters, the classical main conjecture then yields regularized measure generators of the ray class characteristic ideals. The exceptional Teichm\"uller component is treated without the main conjecture: the single Tate correction corresponds to the single pole of the $p$-adic zeta function. At the bottom layer, the local calculation and Herbrand--Ribet yield characterwise nonvanishing criteria involving regularized Bernoulli values. For a single auxiliary prime, the exceptional component detects the Wieferich condition. We also deduce Eisenstein congruence consequences from existing modular-form theorems.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: The distribution of $\alpha p$ modulo one in real quadratic function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.23742v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the thirties of the last century, I.\,M. Vinogradov proved that the inequality $\|p\alpha\|\le p^{-1/5+\varepsilon}$ has infinitely many prime solutions $p$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the distance to a nearest integer. This result has subsequently been improved by many authors. In particular, Vaughan (1978) replaced the exponent $1/5$ by $1/4$, using his celebrated identity for the von Mangoldt function and a refinement of Fourier analytic arguments. The current record is due to Matom\"aki (2009), who showed that the inequality $\|p\alpha\|\le p^{-1/3+\varepsilon}$ has infinitely many prime solutions. This exponent $1/3$ is considered the limit of current technology. Baier and the author established an analogue of Matom\"aki's result for the function field $k=\Fq(T)$ and its imaginary quadratic extensions. Moreover, for real quadratic extensions of $k$ of class number one, they obtained an analogue of Vaughan's result (exponent $1/4$). In this paper, we establish the analogue of Matom\"aki's result for all real quadratic extensions of $k$ without any restriction on the class number.
item.dc:creator: Esrafil Ali Molla

item.title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
item.description: arXiv:2610.37711v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. The values for n <= 5 are classical. We prove D_6 = 107/312, attained only by permutations of (12, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2), and D_7 = 73/180, attained only by permutations of (11, 10, 8, 7, 4, 3, 1). The proof reduces the supremum to a finite search. The key facts are an exact lower bound d_n(v) >= delta^2_U for every rational subspace U perpendicular to v, a matching fiber upper bound, and Banaszczyk's transference theorem, applied along the Korkine-Zolotarev flag of the dual lattice v^perpendicular intersection Z^n. The search is quotiented by signed coordinate permutations and carried out entirely in exact rational arithmetic. It terminates with a certificate: no node of the search is left unresolved, and every surviving candidate is evaluated exactly. The method also recovers the known values for n = 3, 4, 5.
item.dc:creator: Vineet Kahlon

item.title: Distinction and quadratic base change for regular supercuspidal representations
item.description: arXiv:2201.00447v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we study Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations based on the machinery developed by Hakim and Murnaghan to study distinguished representations, and the fundamental work of Kaletha on parameterization of regular supercuspidal representations. For regular supercuspidal representations, we give some new interpretations of the numerical quantities appearing in Prasad's formula, and reduce the proof to the case of tori. The proof of Prasad's conjecture then reduces to a comparison of various quadratic characters appearing naturally in the above process. We also have some new observations on these characters and study the relation between them in detail. For some particular examples, we show the coincidence of these characters, which gives a new purely local proof of Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of these groups. We also prove Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of G(E), when E/F is unramified and G is a general tamely ramified quasi-split reductive group.
item.dc:creator: Chuijia Wang

item.title: A proof of Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2302.08346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that an $n\times n$ circulant Hadamard matrix must satisfy a family of congruence equations that have solutions only when $n \leq 4$, proving Ryser's 1963 conjecture that no such matrices exist for $n>4$.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Morris

item.title: Turning non-smooth points into rational points
item.description: arXiv:2402.14969v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a recent paper, the author and St\"ohr established a bound on the number of iterated Frobenius pullbacks needed to transform a non-smooth purely inseparable point on a regular geometrically integral curve into a rational point. In this paper we improve this result, by establishing a new bound that is sharp in every characteristic $p>0$.
item.dc:creator: Cesar Hilario

item.title: Combinatorial identities derived from explicit formulas of Gauss hypergeometric functions
item.description: arXiv:2607.10643v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the present paper, with the help of the Fa\`a di Bruno formula and several identities of partial Bell polynomials, the author establishes explicit formulas of the Gauss hypergeometric functions \begin{gather*} {\,}_2F_1\biggl(\frac{1-n}{2},\frac{2-n}{2};\frac{3}{2}-m;z^2\biggr), \quad {\,}_2F_1\biggl(-\frac{n}{2},\frac{1-n}{2};\frac{1}{2}-m;z^2\biggr),\\ {\,}_2F_1\biggl(a,a+\frac{1}{2};\frac{3}{2}-m;z^2\biggr), \quad {\,}_2F_1\biggl(a,a+\frac{1}{2};\frac{1}{2}-m;z^2\biggr) \end{gather*} for $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $a\in\mathbb{C}$, and then derives two combinatorial identities \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=0}^{m}\frac{2^k}{k!} \binom{2m-2k}{m-k} \sum_{\ell=0}^{k} \frac{(-1)^\ell}{2^\ell} \frac{(2k-2\ell-1)!!}{(n-\ell)!} \binom{2k-\ell-1}{\ell-1} =\frac{1}{n!}\binom{2m-n}{m} \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=1}^{m}\frac{1}{(k!)^2}\binom{2m-2k}{m-k} \sum_{\ell=1}^{k} \binom{k}{\ell}\ell(2k-\ell-1)! (2a)_\ell =\binom{2m+2a}{m}-\binom{2m}{m}, \end{equation*} where $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $a\in\mathbb{C}$. These newly-established identities extend and generalize the beautiful combinatorial identity \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{2^{k}}{k!}\binom{2n-2k}{n-k} \sum_{j=0}^{k}\frac{(-1)^{j}}{2^j} \frac{(2k-2j-1)!!}{(n-j)!} \binom{2k-j-1}{j-1} =\frac{1}{n!}, \quad n\in\mathbb{N}_0, \end{equation*} which was obtained in Theorem 4 of the paper "F. Qi, C.-Y. He, and D. Lim, Explicit formulas of two Gauss hypergeometric functions and several combinatorial identities, Discrete Appl. Math. Vol. 393 (2026), 215--229. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dam.2026.06.023."
item.dc:creator: Feng Qi

item.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16760v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Galois coinvariants of the geometric \'etale fundamental group and \'etale cohomology of varieties over a finitely generated field $k$. We establish finiteness properties of these coinvariants for (possibly infinite) Galois extensions $L/k$ such that $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As applications, we obtain finiteness results for $L$-rational torsion points on abelian varieties and \'etale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over number fields.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Steklov

item.title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.38954v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $\phi$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $\rho$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_\rho$, $\overline{\Delta}_\rho$, $IC_\rho$, and $\delta_\rho$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$, which were conjectured to exist by Hansen. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp!}\pi$, and $i_{b!*}\pi$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $\pi$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $\phi$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus, as conjectured by Hansen and Hamann-Lee. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.
item.dc:creator: Nikolas Castro

item.title: Non-Archimedean Rigidity and the Uniform Dynamical Manin--Mumford for $\left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40152v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a uniform form of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for split endomorphisms $\Phi = \left(f_1,\ldots,f_n\right): \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n \to \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where each $f_i$ has degree $d \geq 2$ and at most one $f_i$ is exceptional. Specifically, we bound the number of irreducible components of $\overline{\operatorname{Prep}\left(\Phi\right)\cap V\left(\mathbb{C}\right)}^{\operatorname{Zar}}$ uniformly, depending only on $\left(n,d,\operatorname{deg} V\right)$. We also obtain uniform statements for the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture. Our approach combines a degeneration argument via ultrafilters with a new non-archimedean rigidity theorem, along with the quantitative dynamical Zhang's inequality by Mavraki and the second author.
item.dc:creator: Zhuchao Ji, Jit Wu Yap
